summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic back pain, and a history of anxiety was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and hyperglycemia. Her symptoms were triggered by back pain and anxiety, leading to poor oral intake and elevated blood glucose. She was treated with IV fluids for hypovolemia and hyponatremia, insulin therapy adjusted to avoid hypoglycemia, and lorazepam for anxiety. Her nausea resolved, and she tolerated a normal diet. Back pain was managed with acetaminophen, tizanidine, and a single dose of oxycodone. She was discharged on increased Lantus insulin, with recommendations to follow up with endocrinology, pain management, and mental health services to prevent recurrent admissions.
